description.narrative: Improve policies, laws, regulations, and administrative practices affecting the private sector. Includes reducing barriers to competition and unwarranted distortions to market prices; reducing policy and regulatory barriers to establishing, operating, and closing businesses; strengthening the legal framework surrounding property rights that is fair to both men and women, contract enforcement, and dispute resolution, along with the administration of those laws; reducing incentives for corruption and promoting transparent business practices; strengthening the legal framework surrounding intellectual property rights; and improving laws and regulations affecting the creation, dissemination, and use of technology. It also includes improving policies and regulations affecting technology choices and production behaviors with environmental impacts; and improving policies, laws, and regulations affecting hiring and firing of workers, wages, working conditions, and collective bargaining. Includes support for specific improvements as well as efforts to strengthen the institutions that contribute to designing and implementing further improvements.

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

description.narrative: Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

description.narrative: Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

description.narrative: (Georgia): . ..The U.S. government will continue supporting the GOG's.efforts to address the needs of vulnerable children that are potential victims.of gender-based violence (GBV) through prevention and protection. .Specifically, the activity will continue to strengthen the national response.system to abuse, neglect, exploitation, and other forms of violence against vulnerable.children by further elaborating the National Referral Policy and protocols on.responding to the GBV cases against children; build the capacity of social.workers in addressing the needs of children (including street children);.educate school actors in preventing and detecting the GBV cases in schools; and.focus on prevention of GBV and other forms of exploitation and abuse against.children under state custody in small group homes. Support for civil.dialogue and media campaigns will continue in order to enhance the awareness of.the general public and increase the interest of professionals to ensure the rights.of children who are victims of GBV. .. ..The activity is implemented by Georgia's State Fund for.Prevention and Protection of Victims of Human Trafficking and Gender-Based.Violence (the Fund). The Fund is a Georgian state agency mandated to.provide protection, rehabilitation, referral, and reintegration services to the.victims of GBV across the country. The Fund has the ability to implement planned.interventions in a sustainable manner, with the aim of gradually moving to.self-reliance. .. ..Assistance to meet the needs of vulnerable children promotes.a healthier and more productive population to drive inclusive development (JSP.2.2 and ICS MO 1.2), while also upholding Western principles (JRS 4),.strengthening human rights and countering instability (JSP 1.3). .. .. .

description.narrative: The goal of the Healthy Women in Georgia (HWG) Program was to improve evidence-based, women-friendly and client-focused family planning, reproductive health, and safe delivery services, counseling, and education in target communities. Healthy Woman Georgia piloted the liberalization of family planning services and antenatal care in 44 health facilities in disadvantaged rural and urban communities. This successful pilot was scaled-up to 123 facilities throughout the regions where HWG worked. Because of this success, major policy changes in Georgia were pursued to improve access to FP and ANC nationwide. Finally the project improved overall access and utilization of modern contraceptives through public and private sector initiatives.

description.narrative: (Georgia): The new Energy program will support Georgia's efforts to attract investment in power generation capacity as a means to increase national energy security. It will provide technical assistance and training to ministries of energy and economy, energy institutions, and energy market players to assist Georgia in enhancing the country's energy security. The program will support Georgia in energy market development per Georgia's obligations under the Energy Community Treaty; build the capacity of the Government of Georgia (GOG) and relevant institution(s) to evaluate the fiscal and long-term security impacts of regulatory changes; promote energy investments, primarily in variable renewable energy development; support integration of non-hydro renewable energy into the power system; and provide strategic advisory services to the GOG to increase Georgia's energy security. This support will be provided by providing technical assistance to relevant institutions in drafting laws and regulation; providing training and workshops to build Georgia's capacity to analyze the impact of the new laws and regulations; providing training and organizing exchange visits to build capacity of the energy institutions to operate under the new market structure; delivering advisory services to variable renewable energy (VRE) investors and developers to facilitate investments; facilitating funding for the procurement and installation of relevant equipment to increase VRE production forecasting; and delivering advisory services and training to Georgia's energy sector key institutions to identify and address strategic energy security issues. In summary, this technical assistance will be utilize a holistic approach that will focus on legal and policy advice, investment promotion and deal structuring, engineering and environmental analyses, capacity building, financial planning, and outreach, among others.

title.narrative: Procurement of vehicles for the BMSB

description.narrative: (Georgia): Brown Marmorated Stink Bug (BMSB) is an invasive pest that has caused millions of dollars in damage to Georgia's agriculture sector. It was first identified in Georgia in 2015, at which time BMSB populations were at low levels and did not cause noticeable economic damage to crops. Due to ideal breeding conditions, the BMSB populations in western Georgia dramatically increased between 2015 and 2017 and inflicted significant damage to Georgia's hazelnuts; an important export commodity for Georgia's smallholder farmers. If not contained, the BMSB has the potential to set Georgia back years in its agriculture growth and development. Because of this threat, USAID/Georgia will provide support to the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) of Georgia in implementing its Action Plan to combat BMSB infestation.Using FY2017 resources, USAID/Georgia will procure vehicles for the National Food Agency (NFA) of the MoA to support NFA's efforts in responding to the infestation of the BMSB.

title.narrative: USAID Integrated Pest Management (IPM) in Abkhazia

description.narrative: (Georgia): .Georgia's self-reliance as a critical ally in the Caucasus region is threatened by the Russian occupation of Abkhazia. This program will support the U.S. policy objective of restoring Georgia's territorial integrity by reducing the reliance of Abkhaz farmers on Russia and building their capacity to protect their livelihoods against the brown marmorated stink bug (BMSB) and other pests. Abkhaz farmers' livelihoods have been severely damaged in the past two years by the invasive and rapidly spreading stink bug, which has inflicted damage to crops essential to food security and income including hazelnuts, citrus, and corn...This program provides technical assistance and training to strengthen farmers' ability throughout six districts of Abkhazia to apply integrated pest management (IPM) techniques to protect their crops against agricultural pests and access tools and resources to practice IPM effectively. To institutionalize IPM systems, the program will also provide technical assistance to private sector stakeholders in Abkhazia, including input suppliers...A total of $170,000 in technical assistance will contribute to CAATSA Goal 8; by supporting Abkhaz farmers in this time of crisis and building their capacity to respond to future emergencies, the program will decrease Abkhaz dependence on Russian markets while also projecting American leadership through humanitarian relief (JSP 3.4) and strengthening relations between Georgia and its breakaway region (JRS 3.3). These improved relations will help Georgia restore its territorial integrity, make Georgia a stronger and more stable ally for the United States (ICS Mission Goal 2), and increase U.S. influence in the region...This activity is implemented through a PIO grant with the UN since UN agencies are the only international entities able to operate in Abkhazia with diplomatic status. The use of this PIO as an implementer has been approved by USAID/E&E AA..

description.narrative: Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

description.narrative: USAIDs Independent Living Program helps Georgian society build on the progress it has already made protecting the rights of persons with disabilities, promoting the independent living model so that persons with disabilities can participate more fully in Georgian society. USAID works with local governments in six Georgian municipalities to build capacity, deliver improved public services, and promote independent living as a development objective for supporting persons with disabilities. USAID also promotes the independent living model of support in other municipalities around Georgia.

title.narrative: Capacity Building of the State Audit Office of Georgia (SAO)

description.narrative: (Georgia): Under the PASA the GAO/Center for Audit Excellence will assist the State Audit Office (SAO) in determining and estimating the potential effects associated with audit findings developed while conducting performance audits. While SAO has experience in conducting performance audits, it has not had significant experience in quantifying or estimating the potential or actual effects of its findings.This project will improve the quality of SAO's audit recommendations. The Program will introduce to SAO approaches and methodologies for quantifying and estimating potential or actual effects of its findings and will assist in developing policies and procedures for doing so.Program Objectives:Objective 1: Evaluate the current policies and practices of how SAO assesses the effects and impacts of performance audits and provide findings and recommendations on how to develop/improve them.Objective 2: Prepare the workplan (using the results of the evaluation) that will outline the specific capacity building tasks/activities that the Center of Audit Excellence will perform during the remainder of the project. Potential capacity building activities to be included in the workplan may include training, mentoring, and advisory tasks. As a result of the program, SAO will learn new approaches and methodologies for assessing and quantifying the effects of audit findings, that will improve the quality of audit recommendations, leading to increased number of recommendations implemented/resolved, and overall increase in effectiveness and impact of SAO audits.

description.narrative: Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

description.narrative: Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: Policy, Advocacy and Civil Society Development in Georgia (G-PAC)

description.narrative: The Policy, Advocacy, and Civil Society Development Program in Georgia (G-PAC), a four-year initiative funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). This program aims to strengthen civil societys role in advocating for and influencing the development and effective implementation of public policy reforms. In implementing this program, EWMI will work to strengthen the advocacy and watchdog roles of civil society organizations (CSOs) as advocates for an empowered citizenry; improve public policy discourse, research and analysis leading to the development of viable policy options which reflect the citizenrys needs to government; enhance the institutional capacity of universities in the areas of public policy, public administration and political science; and build coalitions to develop strong networks of CSOs throughout Georgia and strengthen their connections to media, political parties and constituencies.

title.narrative: Judicial Independence and Legal Empowerment Project

description.narrative: (Georgia): USAID's Judicial Independence and Legal Empowerment Project (JILEP) is organized around the following four objectives: strengthen judicial independence, accountability, and professionalism; strengthen the institutional capacity of legal professional associations, legal rights non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and state legal aid; improve legal education; and develop commercial law and practice.In FY 2014, JILEP will work on improving procedures for judicial selection and appointment, judicial examination and discipline. It will help the High School of Justice to improve its transparency and quality of education provided. JILEP will continue supporting the NGO Coalition for Independent and Transparent Judiciary, the Georgian Bar Association, state Legal Aid Service and non-state legal aid providers. JILEP will continue providing support to Georgian law schools to improve their curricula and to strengthen capacity of law professors. JILEP will help drafting and publishing commercial law teaching materials and improve teaching of commercial law subjects.

description.narrative: Improve policies, laws, regulations, and administrative practices affecting the private sector. Includes reducing barriers to competition and unwarranted distortions to market prices; reducing policy and regulatory barriers to establishing, operating, and closing businesses; strengthening the legal framework surrounding property rights that is fair to both men and women, contract enforcement, and dispute resolution, along with the administration of those laws; reducing incentives for corruption and promoting transparent business practices; strengthening the legal framework surrounding intellectual property rights; and improving laws and regulations affecting the creation, dissemination, and use of technology. It also includes improving policies and regulations affecting technology choices and production behaviors with environmental impacts; and improving policies, laws, and regulations affecting hiring and firing of workers, wages, working conditions, and collective bargaining. description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: Women as Agents for Change and Empowerment

description.narrative: The projects goal is to enhance womens political participation, along with economic engagement and self-sustainability through providing grassroots rural, internally displaced and national minority womens access to small scale grants, business counseling, job coaching and banking systems and micro finance institutions. The project is being implemented by the Womens Information Center in cooperation with the Taso Foundation, Association of Young Economists of Georgia, and the Institute for War and Peace Reporting (IWPR), in Tbilisi, Mtskheta-Mtianeti, Kakheti, Samtskhe-Javakheti, Imereti and Gali regions.

description.narrative: The Promoting Gender Equality in Employment project seeks to launch advocacy and awareness initiatives designed to increase gender equality and womens economic empowerment in Georgia and ensure inclusive economic growth in which women participate on an equal basis with men. This is done through mobilizing women to demand enforcement of their rights to equality at different work places; increasing the incentives for employers to comply with the existing non-discrimination provisions in Georgian law and enhancing the current legislative and regulatory framework to increase protection for womens right to equality in the workplace.

title.narrative: Broadening Horizons: Improved Choices for the Professional and Economic Development of Women and Girls

description.narrative: The goal of the program is to have increased involvement in and benefit from educational, professional and economic opportunities for women and girls. The main objectives are: 1) 2,000 women and 1,000 girls in municipalities have increased participation in decision making at community and municipal levels, and 2) 3,000 women and girls in 13 municipalities able to make more informed choices based on increased access to information and services in the areas of education, training, employment, and professional development.

title.narrative: Enhancing Capacity for Low Emissions Development Strategies (EC/LEDS) Clean Energy Program – Phase 1

description.narrative: (Georgia): The USG is supporting the Government of Georgia (GOG) in implementing a Low Emission Development Strategy (LEDS) and meeting Georgia's United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) commitments. EC-LEDS Clean Energy Program will help lower emissions in Georgia through enhanced institutional capacity to implement GHG-reducing policies and increased energy efficiency. With FY 2014 resources, it will deploy a LEDS advisor to assist the GOG in preparing a LEDS by mid-2015 and its implementation plan by 2016; implement pilot renewable and energy efficiency projects in up to four municipalities; assist municipalities to prepare up to four Sustainable Energy Action Plans to meet EU Covenant of Mayors requirements to reduce emissions by at least 20 percent by 2020; institutionalize green building standards; and increase access to financing for low emission technologies. (IM #46199, $1,112,225 direct GCC-CE: $556,112 for LEDS development and planning and $556,113 for energy efficiency.)

title.narrative: Supporting Local Self-Governance Reforms in Georgia

description.narrative: ISFED is one of Georgias leading advocacy and election monitoring organizations. This project works in three main directions: 1) Increased transparency and fairness of local self-government elections through election observation; 2) Strengthened civil society at the local level; and 3) Increased capacity of newly elected municipalities. Recent ISFED initiatives include town hall meetings with elected officials, public opinion research, advocacy workshops, and civic and voter education campaigns.

title.narrative: Georgian-Abkhaz and Georgian-Ossetian People-to-People Reconciliation Project

description.narrative: The purpose of this project is to enhance security, increase community capacity for peacebuilding, and strengthen relationships and cross-conflict collaboration among conflict stakeholders. In the short-term, the project aims to improve living conditions for targeted conflict-affected communities by increasing information, communication and economic opportunities. In the mid- to long-term, the project will facilitate changes in the attitudes and behaviors of key conflict stakeholders, including individuals, communities, authorities and civic society. This systemic shift will lay the foundation for future political agreements.

description.narrative: The goal of the Cross-Disability Inclusion Program is to ensure that all children in Georgia realize their human rights as outlined in the United Nations Declaration of the Rights of the Child. The program will promote the right of a child to develop physically and spiritually in a healthy and normal way, with his/her family, regardless of their physical or mental disabilities. The program will strengthen the advocacy role of Disabled Persons Organizations (DPOs) and family organizations: increase the capacity of all actors to better understand the issues and rights of persons with disabilities (PWDs); and increase the ability of healthcare practitioners, social and healthcare policymakers to ensure appropriate services for PWDs. Monitoring and evaluating mechanisms will be established under this new two year program.

title.narrative: Media for Transparent and Accountable Governance (M-TAG)

description.narrative: (Georgia): M-TAG works with competitively selected group of 14 media organizations throughout Georgia to concurrently increase their capacity in content production, web publishing, and business operations. M-TAG works with media partners to provide fact-based reporting and analysis, thus helping the audience to discern disinformation and propaganda and combat anti-Western sentiment M-TAG supports raising reporting standards across the journalism profession by providing operational funds to Ethics Charter and Multimedia Education Center (MEC), to acquire industry-relevant and hands-on production skills. M-TAG helps media partners keep ethnic minority communities and communities affected by conflict on both sides of Administrative Boundary Line informed and provides them with platforms for expression and exchange of ideas and information.With FY 2019 Funds the program will support regional outlets to disseminate COVID-19 related critical pandemic, social or political information in a timely manner. M-TAG will support regional media outlets, including those covering minority communities with language appropriate content, through content production grants and technical assistance to ensure information about continued vigilance, re-emergence and response and recovery efforts and opportunities is well communicated to Georgia's citizens. M-TAG will also support media outlets to analyze and report of COVID-19 response and recovery efforts and communicate citizen's concerns to decision makers at the local and central levels. M-TAG will continue to assist media outlets to improve their online presence, including website development, multimedia content production, online advertising, analytics, editorial management, and management of online TV studios. In addition, the program will continue to support the Georgian Charter of Journalistic Ethics and the Multimedia Education Center, two key institutions that promote high standards in Georgia's media sector.. .

description.narrative: (Georgia): Momavlis Taoba aims to promote greater civic engagement among young people and to expand and institutionalize secondary school civic education curricula through practical applications. The program works with and supports the Ministry of Education and Science (MES) and other stakeholders to expand the reach of civic education activities to 480 schools (20 percent of all Georgia's schools) throughout the country, improving the quality and scope of school-based civic education as a means to positively influence the knowledge, attitudes and behaviors of youth as active participants in Georgia's democratic society. During the next year, activities will continue working closely with MES officials and Civic Education Department staff to advance their skills and lead the national civic education efforts..With FY 2017 funds, Momavlis Taoba will continue to conduct trainings for civic education teachers and civic club students, support capstone "service-learning" projects as part of the in-school curricula and/or through school-based civic clubs. Activities will also continue support of the Civic Education Teachers' Forum in offering professional development opportunities to civic teachers.

description.narrative: The overall goal of this project is to advance local experts knowledge and to build the institutional capacity in the multidisciplinary field of Addictology (science of addiction) to better tackle the acute problem of drug addiction and its negative consequences to society. Alternative Georgia in partnership with Czech and Georgian universities will increase the collective impact of their long-term initiatives through: the development of drug situation monitoring of the Institute of Addictology; the enhancement of the Institutes research capacity; the creation of specific teaching modules; and the institutional capacity building of the Georgian Association of Addictologists.

title.narrative: Advancing CSO Capacities and Engaging Society for Sustainability (ACCESS)

description.narrative: (Georgia): .USAID's Advancing Civil Society Capacities and Engaging Society for Sustainability (ACCESS) activity works to increase citizen engagement with Georgian civil society organizations (CSOs) from across the democratic spectrum. The activity, improves organizational and technical capacity of CSOs to monitor and influence government policies and processes in a non-partisan manner. ACCESS achieves these outcomes through a combination of small grants, trainings, and technical assistance to local organizations; and by supporting the Network of Centers for Civic Engagement in 10 cities, which operate as politically neutral gathering spaces for public discourse on issues of relevant to the Georgian public. By enabling a more constituent-connected, organizationally mature cadre of CSOs, activities assist CSOs to become legitimate representatives of citizens' concerns.With FY 2019 funds ACCESS will expand COVID-19-related programming to address medium and longer-term implications of the pandemic. ACCESS will work with local organizations to continue to build communities' trust in civil society, demonstrate efficient use of resources and encourage community investment in COVID-19 related activities through volunteerism and community resource mobilization. The activity builds the capacity of the civil society sector to contribute to more transparent and accountable governance (ICS MO 1.1) by facilitating dialogue between citizens and their government about key priorities. This activity aligns with U.S. national security interests and supports the U.S. policy priority of promoting American leadership through balanced engagement and increased partnerships with civil society (JSP 3.3 and JRS 4.1). The activity works to counter Russian soft power that discredits civil society. It mitigates democratic backsliding by ensuring an active citizenry and supports the U.S. goals to advance Georgia's Euro-Atlantic integration... .. .. .

title.narrative: Water Sanitation and Hygiene in Adjara activity

description.narrative: (Georgia): .FY 2018 funds will remove barriers to the full participation.of vulnerable children in the education system. Activities will support.infrastructure modifications that improve sanitary conditions and increase.access for children with disabilities. These funds will assist religious.minority Muslim children and youth living in the remote rural areas of Adjara.who are vulnerable and at-risk on a chronic basis, and whose needs are not.otherwise addressed. Assistance is intended to mitigate adverse.conditions for these populations, namely unacceptably poor conditions at school.sanitary facilities, which directly affect the teaching and learning environment.and health and education outcomes. Activities will also focus on the.development of life skills and involvement of parents, communities, and local.governments in improving conditions for vulnerable children in the remote areas.of Georgia. ..Assistance promoting sanitary conditions in schools for.rural, minority youth, and children with disabilities contributes to the U.S..policy priorities of promoting a healthy, educated, and productive population.(JSP 2.2), and increasing partner resilience to counter malign influence (JSP.1.4 and JRS 3.1). Activities directly contribute to post's objective of.supporting an increasingly stable, integrated, and healthy society (ICS MO.1.2)....

title.narrative: Promoting Rule of Law in Georgia (PROLoG)

description.narrative: (Georgia): .USAID will support development of the Georgian justice system to ensure effective implementation of due process and the protection of human rights. Assistance will eliminate barriers that prevent people from understanding and exercising their rights whether those barriers are enshrined in legislation or stem from defective practices; and will work on both the supply and demand sides of governance in the broader rule of law (RoL) sector. Assistance will improve management of justice system institutions, working with judicial leadership to implement new reforms as well as individual courts to improve court efficiency. It will enhance the capacity of legal professionals through training and professional exchange opportunities and support state and civil society to improve access to justice for marginalized groups. Through technical assistance and provision of small grants, the activity will develop mechanisms for the protection of rights, and effective resolution of disputes through capacity building and training of justice system players, and enhanced civil society monitoring of justice system institutions. Activities will promote better protection of gender equality by justice system agencies... ..The entire activity contributes to CAATSA Goal 2. By developing the RoL sector, assistance will advance Georgia on its path to self-reliance, strengthen U.S. strategic partnership with Georgia and help it further integrate with the West as a more democratic and stable country (ICS Mission Goal 1.1). Georgia's success bolsters U.S. leadership and influence in the region serving as a positive example to neighbors of the benefits of pursuing a Euro-Atlantic integration path. An efficient judiciary in Georgia will advance economic security for American investments (JSP 2.3) through effective contract enforcement, fair competition policies and commercial law. Activities are coordinated with Embassy partners as outlined in the Embassy's Justice Sector Strategy... .

title.narrative: Promotion of Integration, Tolerance and Awareness (PITA)

description.narrative: (Georgia): .USAID's diversity-centered program advances the culture of tolerance and inclusive democracy across all segments of Georgian society in order to support stability, broad based economic growth, and a more sustainable democracy. FY 2018 funds will promote civil monitoring mechanisms of the Georgian government programs affecting ethnic and religious minorities; further advance institutional capacities of the Tolerance Center, Council of Ethnic Minorities, and Council of Religions under the Public Defender's Office (PDO); continue to build local NGO capacity to effectively manage and facilitate diversity; support 14 Youth Centers across the country; and work with media professionals on promoting tolerance and equality. Activities encourage social and cultural engagement between majority and ethnic and religious minority groups to dispel misperceptions and eventually permit the collaboration of all groups, laying the foundation for a more sustainable democracy in Georgia. By enshrining human rights and encouraging inclusive development, this activity counters instability (JSP 1.3 and JRS 3.1); promotes healthy, educated, and productive populations (JSP 2.2); and strengthens the effectiveness and sustainability of our investment (JSP 4.1). The activity advances Georgia's western orientation (JRS Goal 4), addresses root causes of global instability, and counters Russian influence by promoting the integration of Georgia's ethnic and religious minorities into the mainstream socio-economic life of Georgia, which also helps prevent the radicalization of marginalized populations. .. .. .

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

description.narrative: Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

title.narrative: Supporting Youth Enterpreneurial Skills for Advancing Employability and Income Generation in Georgia

description.narrative: (Georgia): Nearly a third of all Georgian youth are unemployed. The dearth of employment opportunities and access to capital creates a generation that is economically vulnerable, at risk, and more likely to migrate to Tbilisi or abroad. To address youth unemployment, USAID has forged a public private partnership with the Georgian microfinance institution, Crystal. The program empowers Georgia's young people (17 - 25 years old) by encouraging innovation, promoting entrepreneurship, and enhancing youth employability through skills training, confidence building, and mentoring. The program also operates a Youth Micro Equity Facility that funds youth-led business start-ups. YES will support several high impact workforce development interventions, including: 1) Youth entrepreneurship training program that includes "Train of Trainers" and training of beneficiaries; 2) Youth-led start-up financing program that includes no-interest and semi-equity financing; 3) Youth internship program within private companies; and 4) JobFest program, a joint initiative with Georgia's line ministries, which brings hundreds of youth representatives and dozens of public and private companies together to offer young people internship and job opportunities.The program will also target students of tenth, eleventh and twelve grades to promote Junior Achievement Georgia (JAG)'s business skills education curriculum to public and private high schools. This component aims to develop consumer, economic, social, critical thinking, decision making, problem solving, leadership, and planning skills, which lay the foundation for entrepreneurial skills and prepare pupils for future active life. With FY 2017 resource, the program will engage about 1,800 young people and provide equity financing to create new youth-led businesses.

description.narrative: Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

description.narrative: (Georgia): Hazelnuts are a key cash crop in Georgia, providing livelihoods directly to some 50,000 growers and processors. The Georgia Hazelnut Improvement Project (G-HIP) is a partnership between USAID and Ferrero SpA, representing the overlapping interests of the private sector's commercial activities with USAID's developmental goals. G-HIP is transforming the hazelnut value chain, leveraging expertise and financial support from the private and public sectors to improve hazelnut production and post-harvest handling practices and infrastructure while providing better incomes and employment for rural farmers. G-HIP incentivizes farmers to produce high-quality hazelnuts to generate more income and promote USAID/Georgia's CDCS DO3: Inclusive high-value employment opportunities provided through increased economic growth (JRS 2.3). G-HIP promotes Georgia's self-reliance by pooling more than $6 million in public and private resources in support of hazelnut sector (JRS 5.2.1, JSP 3.3) and will provide $350,000 in training and technical assistance to help protect livelihoods of 50,000 vulnerable farmers living near the occupied territory of Abkhazia and promote hazelnut exports to the EU, thereby reducing Georgia's susceptibility to Kremlin pressure (CAATSA Goal 8.) G-HIP targets 20,000 smallholder farmers and 30 hazelnut processors. Technical assistance will build the capacity of local organizations to provide extension and consulting services to their members and reduce reliance on external donors, while building the capacity of the private sector to produce and process higher quality, more valuable hazelnuts. It will continue to co-invest in high tech processing equipment, such as huskers and dryers, to support these goals. G-HIP will continue to modernize the Georgian hazelnut sector with a focus on traceability and quality-based pricing systems. USAID plans to transition out of the hazelnut sector by the end of the 2020-2025 CDCS strategy period..

title.narrative: Strengthening Political and Electoral Environment for Democracy in Georgia (SPEED)

description.narrative: (Georgia): The purpose of the Strengthening Political and Electoral Environment for Democracy in Georgia project is to conduct credible electoral and political process monitoring activities for the election cycle in Georgia, which includes 2016 Parliamentary, 2017 local, and 2018 Presidential elections and to inform the public of their recommendations in order to help engage citizens in electoral and political processes. ..With FY 2017 funds, activities will continue:.Providing impartial assessment of the elections and political developments based on sound and credible election observation methodology;Increasing awareness of electoral processes among the citizens of Georgia and other target stakeholders by providing the monitoring findings through periodic reports and statements; andContributing to the advancement of political processes in Georgia by developing and following up on recommendations for an improved electoral framework.

title.narrative: Promoting More Competitive, Fair and Inclusive Electoral Environment for 2016-2018 Election Cycle in Georgia

description.narrative: (Georgia): Promoting More Competitive, Fair and Inclusive Electoral Environment for 2016-2018 Election Cycle in Georgia activity works towards improving systemic, legislative, and institutional safeguards for a transparent and free electoral process through the use of monitoring and legal assistance mechanisms. With FY 2017 funds the activity will monitor and report on the work of law enforcement bodies and courts during the local election period. It will deliver evidence-based recommendations to improve the election environment. The activity will promote uniform electoral dispute litigation and empower independent candidates through providing legal support on strategic cases. It will also engage in monitoring and research-based advocacy with the aim to increase compliance of Georgian legislation and practice with international election standards. The activity will work towards increasing the competitiveness of elections by engaging women, persons with disabilities and ethnic minorities.

description.narrative: (Georgia): Russian occupation of Abkhazia and South Ossetia, borderization along these regions, and discontent in communities with ethnically or religiously marginalized populations are direct threats to Georgia's economic and political stability. By building economic resilience in communities along the administrative boundary line (ABL) and regions with marginalized populations, the Zrda program directly counters malign Kremlin influence, contributes to ongoing economic activity along the ABL, and supports Georgia to restore its territorial integrity...Zrda will build the economic resilience of more than 80 communities by supporting at least 800 micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) to acquire equipment and certifications to increase productive capacity and meet international quality standards for goods and services. Zrda will also support the GOG agencies to promote new technologies and innovation; strengthen the public and private sector extension systems; extend digital marketing and electronic matchmaking services between buyers, producers, and service providers; and develop public-private partnerships to build economic opportunities in targeted communities. In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, Zrda will support Georgia's hospitality businesses across 17 municipalities to implement required sanitary regulations...Zrda will provide $1.3 million in training, grants, and technical assistance to advance USAID/Georgia's CDCS DO1: Resilience to external malign influence strengthened (CAATSA Goal 8) and DO3: Inclusive high-value employment opportunities through increased economic growth. By co-investing with the private sector and the GOG to incentivize new business development along the ABL (JRS 2.3.1), Zrda ensures effectiveness to the American taxpayer (JSP 4), promotes American leadership through balanced engagement (JSP 3.3), and mobilizes additional resources to advance Georgia's self-reliance (JRS 5.2.1)... .. .

title.narrative: Waste Management Technologies in Regions (WMTR) – Phase II

description.narrative: (Georgia): .The USAID Waste Management Program supports the Government of Georgia (GOG) in its effort to comply with the environment-related requirements of Georgia's Association Agreement with the European Union (EU). In close cooperation with central and local government agencies, the program introduces modern solid waste management systems and practices throughout Georgia. The program also provides capacity building support for GOG agencies and actively cooperates with the private sector to improve the enabling environment for recycling businesses...With FY 2019 resources, the program will provide technical assistance to the GOG in the closure of old landfills and illegal dumpsites; establish waste separation systems; develop a new tariff scheme for waste management services; implement waste management action plans including those focusing on waste separation and recycling; and provide small grants to nascent recycling enterprises and other sectoral businesses that contribute to a circular economy. The program will also support public information campaigns to promote recycling schemes and a green economy. ..The program will tackle the gaps between Georgia's relatively lax environmental regulations and the rather strict regulations to which Georgia must approximate. The program ensures effectiveness and accountability to the American taxpayer (JSP 4.1) by engaging with Georgian private businesses (JSP 3.3) to reduce waste and implement the Extended Producers' Responsibility (EPR) legislation that requires that manufacturers and importers bear responsibility for the environmental impacts of their products. The program also promotes inclusive and sustainable economic growth (ICS MO 2.1 and JRS 2.2) and Georgia's journey to self-reliance (JSP 3.1 and JRS 5.2.1) as assistance will strengthen the private sector, public sector, and civil society actors to implement Georgia's commitments to the EU..

description.narrative: The Georgia Microfinance Stabilization and Enhancement Activity (GMSE) aims to create stable and operationally sustainable Microfinance Institutions (MFIs), including rural credit in Georgia. It provides funds, technical assistance and training to increase the stability of selected institutions in Georgia through the emulation of best practices worldwide. description.narrative: (Georgia): The purpose of the New Economic Opportunities (NEO) initiative is to improve rural incomes, reduce poverty levels, improve food security, and address critical, small-scale infrastructure constraints in over 80 communities across Georgia. To achieve these goals, NEO supports community level economic development planning, rural economic development, income-generating activities for highly vulnerable groups, and interventions that enable internally displaced persons (IDP) to sustainably maintain their households. With FY 2014 funds, NEO will continue assisting 55 communities along the administrative boundary line (ABL) with South Ossetia, and further expand its small-scale infrastructure and income generating activities along the ABL. Specifically, NEO will implement 20 small-scale infrastructure activities (e.g., potable water systems, irrigation channels, drainage, tertiary roads) benefiting up to 4,000 households; deliver vocational training, interest free and/or low interest micro loans and trade-specific toolkits; and support the development of beekeeping, fruit/vegetable production, apparel-making, hairdressing, and a variety of construction and agricultural practices, benefiting at least 2,000 households. Approximately $50,000 of FY 2014 resources will be used to develop functioning value chains with a special focus on benefiting vulnerable populations.

description.narrative: (Georgia): .The Georgia Primary Education Project (G-PriEd) provides comprehensive assistance to the primary education system in Georgia to improve reading and math competencies and develop business skills of Georgian and ethnic minority students. G-PriEd supports up to 560 public schools in improving methods of instructions. Activities include increasing the availability of language- and age-appropriate reading and math materials; enhancing testing and classroom assessment tools; promoting the use of new technologies; and engaging parents and communities in the instructional process. G-PriEd will allow the target schools to provide continuous training and in-service support to 8,000 teachers; improve reading and math competencies of 40,000 primary grade students; support reading and math clubs with parents' engagement; and expand the current reach of the program to additional 1,000 students to promote a school-based acquisition of business skills among learners at primary grades..

description.narrative: (Georgia): The Restoring Efficiency to Agriculture Production (REAP) activity supports the development of commercially sustainable and competitive enterprises in agriculture to increase incomes and employment in rural areas. REAP delivers firm-level investment and technical assistance to expand the operations of existing smallholder farmers and rural enterprises. The program also facilitates the entry of new agribusinesses and input suppliers, including machinery service providers, storage facilities, sorting/grading centers, and processors. REAP catalyzes commercial finance to the sector and expands sustainable linkages among service providers, producers, post-harvest enterprises and local consulting firms. With FY 2016 funds, as reflected in Georgia's Feed the Future Scale-up Plan, REAP will support the expansion of 30 privately-run machinery and farm service centers to provide access to fee-based machinery services, agricultural inputs, and demonstration plots for 35,000 farmers.

description.narrative: (Georgia): .With FY 2018 funds, G4G will provide technical assistance and training to the Georgian government, private sector, business associations, academic institutions, and think tanks to support Georgia's efforts to develop a predictable business environment in which legal and regulatory frameworks are fairly and transparently applied. To promote transparency and accountability in the reform-making process, G4G will facilitate public-private dialogues on topics such as EU integration, energy market trading, water resource allocation, insolvency, and capital market reform... ..With G4G support, Georgia passed legislation that mandates the Georgian government to undertake Regulatory Impact Assessments (RIA) for all major policy changes or laws starting January 1, 2019. While the RIA process is now institutionalized on paper, the full economy- and government-wide adoption of RIAs may take some time. G4G will ensure effectiveness and accountability to the American taxpayer (JSP 4.1) by undertaking RIAs of priority reforms while providing coaching and peer review assistance to build the culture for evidence-based analysis that will last beyond the life of the project... ..G4G will also support the Georgian government to analyze transaction settlement options for the newly-liberalized energy market, develop a training course on taxation for vocational students, provide training and technical assistance to the Revenue Service on post clearance audits for authorized economic operators, support the Georgian government in the implementation of the pension law communication strategy, and assess opportunities for adopting innovative digital tools, such as blockchain, in line with Georgian government's digital government initiatives. These market-oriented reforms will create a predictable business environment, expand business opportunities for Georgia's citizens (ICS MO 2.1 and JRS 2.2), and create a better market for U.S. exports and investment (JSP 2.3 and JRS 2.1)..

description.narrative: (Georgia): .Good Governance Initiative (GGI) is designed to support the GOG in strengthening transparency, accountability, and effectiveness of select governance and service delivery systems to achieve: improved administrative and financial management of public institutions; improved access to independent, reliable and balanced information on government performance; strengthened policy development and lawmaking; and strengthened institutional oversight of GOG. GGI's government counterparts include the Prime Minister's Office; the Ministries of Finance, Health, Justice, and Regional Development; Parliament; the State Audit Office; Public Defender's and State Inspector's Offices and select local governments. Interventions will work with government and civil society representatives to enhance public participation, public awareness and monitoring of public administration and parliamentary strengthening reforms. The activity will have emphasis on COVID19 response. ..Using FY 2019 funds, GGI's activities will be focused on:.Supporting the GoG in COVID19 response through policy research in the governance areas impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic; analysis of government operations during the pandemic; mapping of public services and developing recommendations for operationalizing essential public services to be accessible remotely; developing guidelines for the operation of civil service during the crisis; supporting remote operations of the Parliament; etc. Supporting the implementation of the Local Government Decentralization Strategy (2020-2025) by providing necessary technical assistance in select areas.Supporting the implementation of Anti-Corruption Action Plan (2019-2020) and Open Government Partnership Action Plans in select municipalities.Improving state oversight through supporting the Parliament and the State Audit Office as well as building internal control functions of the government agencies... .

description.narrative: This project builds upon the comprehensive assessment of teaching, training and research needs in the Georgian agricultural sector that was commissioned by the United Nations Development Program (UNDP) in late 2011. The project will establish a concentration in Agricultural Economics within the International School of Economics at Tbilisi University (ISET) Masters Program in Economics. Selected second year ISET students will complete courses focused on agricultural market analysis, trade in agricultural goods, and agricultural policy. The project will also establish an Agricultural Policy Research Center (APRC) at ISETs Policy Institute. This new center will develop and communicate relevant research, deliver on-demand consulting services, training, policy evaluation and analysis, thus contributing to the projects sustainability. The projects aim is to create a pool of well-trained young economists capable of addressing a wide array of issues related to agricultural and rural development policy in Georgia and the region. Several cohorts of well-trained agricultural economists educated through this project will be employed by the Ministry of Agriculture, other public agencies, NGOs, businesses and international organizations concerned with agricultural policy and Georgias rural development.

description.narrative: (Georgia): The Youth Participation and Development (YPD) project supports youth engagement and participation in conflict-affected areas of Georgia to enhance social integration of young people by promoting confidence building and empowerment of young people.Using FY 2015 funds, the project will strengthen the capacities of teachers, peer educators, youth club facilitators and members to improve chances for a sustainable development of youth clubs and enhance communication lines among youth from the conflict affected regions. The project will cover the cross-cutting areas of math, science and technology, environment, healthy lifestyles and civic education. The project will promote school-based and extra-curricular activities. YPD also supports small scale community-based projects that include capacity development, youth leadership, and youth participation through thematic workshops, conferences, community outreach activities, curriculum upgrade/development, as well as provision of equipment and other supplies.

description.narrative: (Georgia): .With FY 2018 funds, USAID will assist the Georgian government in piloting and developing a nationwide Functional Assessment System for children with disabilities. The system will facilitate distribution of assistance and services for persons with disabilities (PWDs) by capturing accurate data and realistically assessing the needs of PWDs. This activity will establish a pilot system in the Adjara region. All new applicants seeking the status of a person with disability will take the function assessment (approximately 2500 individuals). All 16 primary and secondary medical care instructions in Adjara, currently providing medical examinations to the disability status applicants, will be engaged in the pilot. UNICEF will train over 200 professionals in these institutions to administer functional assessments. UNICEF will also provide monitoring of the pilot and analyze the pilot data to provide recommendations for the country-wide scale up of the functional assessment system in the coming years. .USAID and EU are funding the functional assessment pilot. The EU will contribute about 10 percent and USAID - 90 percent of resources required for development and implementation of the pilot. ..The activity will be non-competitively added as an expansion to a current award implemented by UNICEF, after the approval of a Senior Obligation Alignment Review (SOAR). Given that UNICEF has in-depth, county-specific knowledge, and GOG specifically requested UNICEF's assistance in this area, a PIO agreement with UNICEF is the best approach to carry out this work in Georgia....The Functional Assessment System of persons with disabilities is one of the Georgian government's commitments in the EU Association Agreement that will advance the U.S. policy priority of promoting healthy and productive populations in a partner country (JSP 2.2 and ICS MO 1.2)....... .. .. .. .

title.narrative: Horizons Enhanced Engagement with the Occupied Territories (Horizons)

description.narrative: (Georgia): With FY19 funds, USAID will provide opportunities for dialogue and confidence-building between youth and professionals in Abkhazia and across the administrative boundary line (ABL) through the Horizons activity. Interventions will work to counter Kremlin influence in Abkhazia by challenging divisive propaganda and disinformation, and develop mechanisms that further link communities across the ABL. The activity will combat dependence on Russian patronage by providing training and technical assistance to strengthen skills in IT, math, science, foreign languages, and civics; improve healthcare; support Business Education Centers; and encourage development of innovative value chains. The activity develops grassroots mechanisms for cross-ABL interaction and creates opportunities to change perceptions and behaviors to overcome the conflict paradigm and potential openings for reconciliation by facilitating relationships between youth and professionals to engage on topics such as education, health, science and technology. . UN agencies enjoy a unique position as a trusted interlocutor by both the GOG and community leaders in Abkhazia. Therefore, UNDP has a significant comparative advantage in the technical areas outlined above that require cooperation not only from individuals but also community institutions. .The entire activity directly aligns with the U.S. policy priority to strengthen the resilience of our partners to deter malign Kremlin influences (JSP 1.4 and JRS 3.1). The activity seeks the peaceful resolution of protracted conflict through more stable communities and increased engagement around common challenges (ICS MO 1.2). This activity directly supports CAATSA Goal 3 by responding to the humanitarian crises and instability caused or aggravated by the invasion and occupation of Georgia by the Russian Federation.. .

description.narrative: (Georgia): The Waste Management Technologies in Regions activity will improve policy formulation and strategic planning related to waste management at national and local levels in Georgia; enhance the capacity of targeted municipalities to establish and sustainably manage waste facilities and services; and support the development of Georgia's recycling sector. It will develop remediation plans for old and illegal landfills, which will improve management on thousands of hectares of land. The activity will help reduce environmental pollution, improve sanitation and human health, and increase the quality and quantity of recycled products.With FY 2014 resources, the activity will train selected Georgian municipalities and waste management companies in waste collection and recycling systems, assist them with developing business plans for waste management and alternative tariff structures for waste collection services, and implement public awareness campaign to educate the populace about proper waste management practices.

description.narrative: (Georgia): The purpose of Strengthening Electoral Processes (SEP) is to deepen and institutionalize Georgia's electoral processes by enhancing professional oversight of elections and increasing civic engagement. Specifically, with FY 2015 funds SEP will improve the Government of Georgia capacity to administer and oversee free and fair electoral processes. Areas of intervention include reforming the electoral legislative framework, improving the capacity of the election management body through strategic planning, and creating a more inclusive process to election administration. It will also enhance civic engagement around key electoral and political process reforms. The Democracy and Citizenship course at the university level will expand to more than 22 universities and work to build the capacity of local civil society organizations to take over the administering of the course. Additionally, SEP will provide assistance to gender advocacy groups and disability rights organizations for capacity building on voter education initiatives.

title.narrative: Strengthening Political Processes (SPP) - Strengthening Political Parties - in Georgia

description.narrative: (Georgia): Strengthening Political Processes (SPP) activity works to deepen and institutionalize Georgia's political processes by continuing to build the capacity of political parties at the national and local levels. This high level result will be achieved by improving the organizational capacity and intra-party democracy of political parties through a scorecard method. One- and two-day training was developed following an analysis of the scorecard administered for each party. Using FY 2017 funds, training will cover various topics from strategic planning and communication to inclusion and women's leadership skills. In addition, focus is placed on improving parties' communication and engagement with their regional branches.

description.narrative: (Georgia): Georgia Agricultural Policy Initiative (GAPI) assists the Ministry of Agriculture of Georgia (MOA) to develop an effective agricultural information system and create a policy unit to conduct market outlook and agricultural policy analysis. GAPI will support MOA to develop the data necessary for conducting analytical policy work in market outlook analysis, supply and demand analysis, and the construction of food balance sheets. GAPI's technical assistance and training for MOA will focus on prioritizing data needs, and designing data collection procedures to fulfill the most important agricultural data needs of Georgia. GAPI will also provide training in market outlook analysis of commodities important to Georgia's economy and assist in developing and conducting surveys for aquaculture production and production in greenhouses. Finally, GAPI will help MOA to implement objective yield surveys for wheat, apples and citrus, and monitor the corn objective yield survey.

title.narrative: Performance Evaluation of the Georgia Education Management Project

description.narrative: IBTCI led a performance evaluation of the three-year (June 2009-July 2012) $5.7 million Georgia Education Management Project (EMP). The purpose of the evaluation was to examine whether the EMP project was effective in achieving its results in terms of introducing a new formula for school financing, developing the Education Management Information System (EMIS) for the Ministry of Education and Science (MES); and establishing the first Master of Education (M.Ed.) in Educational Administration program in a Georgian university. USAID plans to use the evaluation results to understand the current state of the management of the education system in Georgia and changes brought about by the project and to assist it in planning future education sector activities. The results were shared with other education sector stakeholders inside and outside of Georgias Ministry of Education and Sciences to assist them in understanding the impact of EMP and in planning their own activities.

title.narrative: Evaluation of Civil Society and Media Programs

description.narrative: IBTCI has been contracted by USAID/Georgia to conduct mid-term project performance evaluations for the following two programs in Georgia: Policy, Advocacy and Civil Society Development in Georgia (G-PAC) and; Georgian Media Enhance Democracy, Informed citizenry and Accountability (G-MEDIA). The evaluations assess the extent to which the intended results of both projects have occurred and look at the major impediments to achieving some of the results, and how the interventions can be improved to ensure achievement of projects end results. The results of the evaluation will be used by USAID/Georgia for making mid-course adjustments to both programs to increase their effectiveness and ensure the achievement of intended end results.

description.narrative: (Georgia): HICD 2020 activity provides consultancy services to the.U.S. government's strategic partner organizations facing administrative.limitations and management inefficiencies that impede effective implementation.of key reforms of the government of Georgia, including those related to the.European Union Association Agreement and the Open Government Action Plan. Every.year, USAID's implementing partners submit proposals for HICD support to.nominated government or nongovernmental organizations who play a critical role.in advancing the U.S. government's development assistance objectives. USAID.selects organizations for HICD support based on the following criteria: relevance.(assistance must address institutional performance), strategic fit, synergies.with existing technical assistance efforts, sustainability, and institution's commitment.and buy-in. Key activities include holistic.assessments of selected organizations' internal systems, operations, and policies;.rectifying identified issues (e.g., in organizational structures, management.systems, human resources and financial management, etc.) through training and.advisory services; and monitoring the organizations' continued.performance. Using FY 2018 funds, the activity will continue assistance.to the following entities: National Food Agency, International Society.for Fair Elections and Democracy, Multimedia Education Center, Georgian Waste.Management Association, Georgian National Communications Commission, State Fund.for Protection and Assistance of Victims of Human Trafficking, State.Procurement Agency, and will select new institutions for assistance...By improving the organizational capacity of selected.organizations the activity contributes to the country's ability to plan,.finance, and implement solutions to solve its own development challenges (JSP.4.1 and JRS 5.4); and it enhances democratic checks and balances and.accountable governance (ICS MO 1.2) in Georgia... ... ...

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

description.narrative: The goal of the Georgia HIV Prevention Project (GHPP) is to support HIV prevention among high-risk groups in order to avert the spread of HIV to the general population. GHPP works with a number of local nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) to develop and implement HIV prevention activities for most-at-risk populations (MARPs). The project works at the individual, community, societal, and policy levels to reduce HIV-related stigma and discrimination in Georgia.

title.narrative: Cooperation in Health Systems Transformation Project (CoReform)

description.narrative: The Cooperation in Health Systems Transformation Project (CoReform) provides technical assistance to the Government of Georgia to build its capacity to transform the countrys health system into one that is more efficient, accountable and transparent. With overarching ownership from the Ministry of Labor, Health and Social Affairs (MoLHSA), along with the CoReform team led by Abt Associates Inc., the project is designed to help the Government of Georgia improve its healthcare financing system, support reproductive health and family planning (RH/FP) and strengthen health institutions at the national level. Activities aim to help the Government of Georgia to adopt innovative and comprehensive solutions for the equity and affordability gaps in the health system, high abortion rates and limited donor coordination.

title.narrative: USAID Interagency Agreement with USDA Forest Service

description.narrative: (Georgia): USAID in partnership with U.S. Forest Service (USFS) will provide technical assistance for natural resource management to Georgian government agencies, including the Ministry of Environmental Protection, Forestry Agency, Ministry of Agriculture, and environmental NGOs. Georgia is currently reorganizing forest sector policies and institutions, and hiring a new cadre of forestry personnel. USFS technical assistance for these efforts will include training and advisory services on sustainable forest management with resulting benefits for biodiversity, economic development, governance and institution building objectives. Technical assistance will also be provided to rural communities to improve grazing practices to address erosion and mitigate the risk of natural disasters such as mudslides and floods in rural Georgia. This activity will support the effective management of forest resources, including improved planning and enforcement of practices, which is expected to reduce unsustainable logging practices and retention of forest coverage resulting in the reduction of emissions and climate change mitigation. This activity also indirectly contributes to climate change adaptation objectives as it works to address poor forestry, grazing, and rural road construction practices in Georgia that create increased erosion, resulting in polluted watersheds/rivers and increased risks for natural disasters, including mudslides, landslides, and floods. Proper forest management will make forests more resilient in the face of climate change. (IM#54074 $630,000 Indirect GCC-SL; and $120,000 Indirect GCC-AD.)This assistance contributes to the biodiversity earmark and focuses on the entire territory of Georgia, including the autonomous region of Adjara but excluding the breakaway regions of Abkhazia and South Ossettia.
